quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 CALL - HEADLINE: record fourth-quarter sales of $6.439 billion, up 49% in US dollars and 37% organically, with sales and adjusted EPS both 'exceeding the high end of our guidance'; adjusted operating margin 27.5%, up 510 basis points YoY and matching the third quarter's record. Record orders of $8.4 billion, up 68% YoY and 38% sequentially, for a book-to-bill of 1.31 to one - the CFO: 'primarily driven by robust bookings in the IT datacom market related to AI applications.' Full year 2025: sales approximately $23.1 billion (+52% in US dollars, +38% organic), orders $25.4 billion (+51%, book-to-bill 1.1 to one), record adjusted operating margin 26.2%. The CEO: 'we're very proud to have more than doubled Amphenol's revenues in the past four years.'
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 sales $6.439 billion (+49% USD, +37% organic); orders $8.4 billion (+68% YoY, +38% sequential), book-to-bill 1.31 to one; adjusted operating margin 27.5%; FY2025 sales $23.1 billion (+38% organic), orders $25.4 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - IT DATACOM (THE AI SEGMENT) WAS 38% OF Q4 SALES and 36% of full-year 2025 sales. Q4 IT datacom sales grew 'by a very strong 110% in US dollar and organic driven by continued strong demand for our products used in AI applications together with ongoing growth in our base IT datacom business'; sequentially +8%, 'substantially better than our expectations ninety days ago', and 'This sequential increase was essentially driven by growth in AI-related applications.' Communication Solutions segment Q4 sales were $3.4 billion (+78% in US dollars, +60% organic) at a 32.5% segment operating margin. Q1 2026 outlook for IT datacom: a 'low double-digit sequential sales increase in the first quarter driven by the addition of CommScope', roughly flat organically - an analyst called it 'flattish organically excluding CCS'; the CEO replied 'you're correct' and noted 'Traditionally, the base IT datacom cycle would be down in the first quarter.'
quarterly_data.figure: IT datacom 38% of Q4 sales (36% of FY2025); Q4 +110% USD and organic; +8% sequential (AI-driven); Communication Solutions Q4 sales $3.4 billion (+60% organic), 32.5% segment margin

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - WHY THE RECORD 1.31 BOOK-TO-BILL, AND CUSTOMERS SHARING THE CAPACITY RISK: the CEO said 'the IT datacom market specifically related to AI investment was a primary driver of this 1.31 book-to-bill and record orders', with book-to-bill at or above one in every end market but perhaps one. 'We have seen customers open up their order window for in particular related to significant plans that they have of investments related to AI. This is not because of kind of getting in line.' Because next-generation products are 'really pushing the limits of these systems', they 'require, in certain cases, more automation' (Amphenol does 'the vast majority of that in-house'), so Amphenol works with customers 'to somehow share the risk of those investments': 'Those ways can include customers actually sharing some of the spending, contributing to the spending, and, otherwise, you know, giving us commitments that are solid commitments' - 'I wouldn't call it minimum order.' Later in Q&A: 'these are really outstanding orders, and they will carry through longer than just here in the first quarter.' No customers named.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill 1.31 (AI-driven); customer co-funding and solid commitments behind capacity; orders to carry beyond Q1

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - COMMSCOPE (CCS) CLOSED EARLY; FIRST 2026 CONTRIBUTION OUTLOOK: the CCS business acquired from CommScope closed in January, 'a bit earlier than we had anticipated', and will be known as 'CommScope, an Amphenol company' - bringing 'significant fiber optic interconnect capabilities, for the IT datacom and communications networks markets' plus building-connectivity products (reported in the industrial segment). Management expects CommScope full-year sales of $4.1 billion and 15¢ of accretion to Amphenol's 2026 adjusted EPS. At announcement it was 'a company of roughly $3.6 billion in sales at a 26% EBITDA margin' (just over 11 times); by close 'a business of more than $4 billion in annualized sales' with 'strong orders, positive book-to-bill' - a 'high single digits' EBITDA multiple on a 2026 basis. CFO: CommScope's operating margin is expected 'in the high teens for the full year', a bit under that in Q1 on seasonality ('a bit over a 100 basis point impact' on Q1 company margins), with the target to lift it to the company average. CEO: CCS 'vaults us into a position of breadth and depth in the technology around fiber optic interconnect'; its former parent was 'somewhat balance sheet constrained', while Amphenol is 'more than willing' to make prudent investments to help it grow.
quarterly_data.figure: CommScope 2026 sales $4.1 billion, 15¢ EPS accretion; $3.6 billion at announcement -> more than $4 billion annualized at close; operating margin in the high teens

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - THE AI INTERCONNECT CONTENT THESIS ENTERING 2026: the CEO stressed breadth 'up and down the stack of AI' - 'the big web scale folks', 'the cloud, the Neo cloud', equipment manufacturers, and 'companies who are designing the chips and the architecture around those chips'. Customers' 'investment plans are all going up', and 'upgrades of the technology embedded in those data centers' require 'a higher technology, more complex, higher content degree of interconnect.' Amphenol participates in 'bringing the power in, power to the racks', in 'the data communication within racks, within adjacent racks', and now, with CommScope, in 'the broader fiber optic opportunity' - 'getting a signal from a GPU to a GPU or from a central office home somewhere'. Asked about an eventual move to 800-volt data-center power (the analyst's framing), the CEO answered: 'what we care about, Joe, is that there's more of everything... they go to different voltages. They go to different speeds... The ultimate what comes out of that is more complexity', adding that with CommScope Amphenol is 'even stronger than we were before' to help customers with these trade-offs.

CALL - Q1 2026 GUIDANCE (assuming current market conditions and constant exchange rates): sales in the range of $6.9 billion to $7 billion, 43% to 45% growth YoY, and adjusted EPS of $0.91 to $0.93 (+44% to 48%), including $900 million of sales and $0.02 of adjusted EPS accretion from CommScope. By market: IT datacom up a low double-digit percentage sequentially on the CommScope addition; communications networks up 'a significant nearly 50%' on CommScope, more than offsetting seasonal declines; industrial up approximately 20% from CommScope's building connectivity business. The CFO guided an adjusted tax rate of 25.5% continuing into 2026 and quarterly net interest expense of approximately $200 million after the CCS acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 2026 sales $6.9 billion to $7 billion (43% to 45% growth); adjusted EPS $0.91 to $0.93; includes $900 million of CommScope sales

quarterly_data.signal: CALL - CAPACITY AND COSTS: the CFO said capital spending ended 2025 'just a bit over 4%' of sales, against a historic range of three to 4%, and 2026 capex should be 'at that upper end of that 4% range', with some quarters exceeding 4%, given growth opportunities and the strong Q4 orders. The CEO described operations that 'more than doubled the size of their individual operations', teams 'figuring out how to set up factories in four different countries' and 'ramping up automation machines that we've never built before'; the company operates '350 factories across more than 40 countries'. He called the cost of metals 'extraordinary'; the CFO said that, as of now, metals are not seen 'having any significant impact' on the 2026 margin outlook, with Q1 organic conversion on the seasonal decline in 'the mid-thirties' and a targeted conversion margin of about 30% on incremental sales.
quarterly_data.figure: capex just a bit over 4% of sales in 2025 (historic three to 4% range); 2026 at the upper end of that 4% range; 350 factories across more than 40 countries
